fields.meaning: Despite (opposition)…, overcoming… (を押して)
examples: He played in the match despite being ill.
The two of them got married in the face of opposition from everyone around them.
I decided to study abroad despite my family's objections.

fields.meaning: Since… (a major turning point: を境に)
examples: That incident changed the relationship between the two of them.
Since turning 40, I have begun to feel my physical strength declining.
I haven't seen him since I moved.

fields.meaning: To feel…, to experience… (辛い思いをする)
examples: I had an embarrassing experience on the train.
As a child, I grew up feeling lonely.
I never want to go through anything that frightening again.

fields.meaning: About…; generally…; completely (not) (およそ)
fields.connection: およそ + Quantity / およそ + N
examples: It takes about 20 minutes to get to the station.
That story is not realistic at all.
When it comes to studying in general, what matters is keeping at it.

fields.meaning: As if…, just as though… (さも)
fields.connection: さも + [sentence/clause] + (そうに/そうな) [sentence/clause] + (ように/ような)
examples: He talked as if it were his own achievement.
The cat is sleeping, looking ever so comfortable.
She made a face as if she were really surprised.

fields.meaning: Otherwise… (さもないと)
fields.connection: [sentence/clause] 1 + さもないと さもなければ + [sentence/clause] 2
examples: Leave now. Otherwise you'll be late.
Be quiet. Otherwise I'll have to ask you to leave.
You'd better apologize right now. Otherwise, he probably won't forgive you.

fields.meaning: To miss the chance to…, to fail to… (V+そびれる)
examples: I missed the right moment and never got to say thank you.
I was so busy that I missed lunch.
There's something I didn't get a chance to ask, so I'll contact you again.

fields.meaning: To fail to…, to do… wrong (損なう/損ねる)
examples: I overslept and missed the train.
I phrased it badly and ended up offending him.
Postcards with writing mistakes can be exchanged.

fields.meaning: There is no way to… (術がない)
examples: I don't know his contact details, so I have no way to let him know.
At that time, there was no way to cure this disease.
There is no way to confirm the truth.

fields.meaning: At the very moment… (unintentional: た弾みに/た拍子に)
examples: When I fell, my glasses went flying.
As I stood up, I hit my head.
As I shut the door, I caught my finger in it.

fields.meaning: To treat as having…, to consider as… (たことにする)
examples: Let's pretend we didn't hear what was just said.
Please consider that promise as never having been made.
On paper, the meeting is recorded as having taken place.

fields.meaning: Had no intention of… (たつもりはない)
examples: I didn't mean to hurt you.
I had no intention of lying.
I didn't mean it as an order, but apparently that's how it sounded.

fields.meaning: All one can do is…, there is nothing to do but… (ただ～のみだ)
examples: The preparations are done. All that's left is to wait for the results.
I won't make excuses. All I can do is apologize.
Having come this far, there is nothing to do but press forward.

fields.meaning: It has never once happened that…, never… (ためしがない)
examples: He has never once arrived on time.
This plan has never gone well.
My younger brother has never kept a promise.

fields.meaning: If…, would have… (counterfactual supposition: たら～ところだ)
fields.connection: たら ば なら + [sentence/clause] + V plain form + ところだ
examples: If I had been five minutes later, I would have missed the train.
If you hadn't told me, I would have made a huge mistake.
If I hadn't had insurance, I would have been in serious trouble.

fields.meaning: As a…, one must… (one's position: たる者)
examples: A teacher should set an example for students.
A leader must not give up easily.
A politician should listen to the voice of the people.

fields.meaning: …is only natural, ought to… (てしかるべきだ)
examples: His achievements ought to be valued more highly.
This issue ought to be debated in the Diet.
Shouldn't there be an apology?

fields.meaning: It is not something that can be settled just by… (て済むことではない)
examples: This isn't something that can be settled with an apology.
This isn't something money can solve.
Saying "I didn't know" doesn't make it all right.

fields.meaning: Even if you…, it won't help (てもどうにもならない)
examples: There's no use regretting it now.
Worrying about it on your own won't get you anywhere.
Crying won't solve anything.

fields.meaning: If you…, don't blame me (warning: ても知らない)
examples: If you eat that much and get a stomachache, don't blame me.
If you stay out late and can't get up tomorrow, it's your own fault.
If you won't listen to advice, don't come to me when you fail.

fields.meaning: As if to say… (とばかりに)
examples: He pointed at the door as if to say, "Get out."
She spoke up as if to say, "Now's my chance."
The dog is wagging its tail as if to say it wants to play.

fields.meaning: It could be said that… (と言えなくもない)
fields.connection: V plain form + と言えなくもない / N + (だ/である) / Na + (だ/である) / Aい
examples: You could say his opinion has a point too.
At this price, you could say it's cheap.
It could be said that the responsibility lies with me.

fields.meaning: As soon as one sees that…, immediately… (と見るや)
fields.connection: V plain form + とみるや
examples: As soon as it saw that no customers were coming, the store immediately started cutting prices.
As soon as he saw the situation was unfavorable, he changed his strategy.
The moment she saw her chance, she went all out on the attack.

fields.meaning: All too easily…, tend to… (ともすれば)
examples: When you live alone, your daily routine all too easily becomes irregular.
When people are busy, they tend to neglect their health.
It is easy to forget, but gratitude is important.

fields.meaning: For someone like… to do such a thing (としたことが)
examples: How could I, of all people, forget such important documents?
To think that someone as careful as he is would make a mistake like this.
For a professional to get the basics wrong!

fields.meaning: Instantly, on the spur of the moment (とっさに)
examples: A car was coming, so I instantly jumped out of the way.
When asked my name, I couldn't answer on the spot.
A split-second decision saved a life.

fields.meaning: Even… (とて)
examples: Even parents don't know everything about their children.
Even experts make mistakes sometimes.
Even the company president has to follow the rules.

fields.meaning: Completely different from…, a complete change from… (とは打って変わって)
examples: Unlike yesterday's rain, today is perfectly clear.
In stark contrast to his usual attitude, he was serious.
In complete contrast to last month, sales are rising.

fields.meaning: …completely, …all of (V+尽くす)
examples: He knows that town inside out.
The fire burned all the household belongings to the ground.
I am more grateful than words can express.

fields.meaning: I told you… (reproach: ってば/ったら)
fields.connection: [sentence/clause] + ってば ったら / N + (だ) Na + (だ)
examples: I said I get it already. Stop saying it over and over.
Oh, Mom, you're not listening to me again.
I said I'm going. Just wait a second.

fields.meaning: Doesn't count as…, hardly deserves to be called… (うちに入らない)
fields.connection: V plain form + うちに(は)入らない / N + の / Na / Aい
examples: Rain like this hardly counts as rain.
Three months of studying doesn't count as having studied.
That level of spiciness doesn't even count as spicy.

fields.meaning: Neglecting…, putting… aside (をそっちのけで)
examples: My son is ignoring his homework and playing video games.
He neglects his work and is absorbed in his hobbies.
The meeting agenda was pushed aside, and the small talk went on and on.

fields.meaning: What with… and… (negative listing: わ～わで)
fields.connection: V plain form + わ + V plain form + わ(で) / Aいわ + Aいわ(で) / Naだわ + Naだわ(で)
examples: What with losing my wallet and getting caught in the rain, it was the worst day ever.
What with the train being delayed and being late for the meeting, it was a disaster.
What with the kids crying and the phone ringing, it was chaos.

fields.meaning: As soon as…, immediately… (や否や)
examples: The moment I opened the door, the cat came darting out.
He fell asleep the moment he got into bed.
That product sold out as soon as it was released.

fields.meaning: What with… and… (やれ～やれ～)
fields.connection: やれ + N + だ(の) + やれ + N + だ(の) + と / [sentence/clause] + [sentence/clause]
examples: What with overtime and working on my days off, I haven't had a moment to rest lately.
My mother keeps nagging me: study, clean up your room.
He does nothing but complain: he has a headache, he's tired.

fields.meaning: No matter how… (ようが/ようと)
fields.connection: V (V volitional form) + が と(も) / N + だろう/であろう / Na + だろう/であろう / Aい + かろう
examples: No matter what people say, I don't care.
No matter how expensive it is, I'll buy what I need.
Even if it rains, the match will be held.

fields.meaning: Whether… or… (ようが～ようが)
fields.connection: V (V volitional form) + が と(も) / N + だろう/であろう / Na + だろう/であろう / Aい + かろう
examples: Whether you cry or scream, the decision won't change.
Rain or wind, I run every day.
Whether people oppose me or laugh at me, I'm going to do it.

fields.meaning: Depending on how one… (ようによっては)
examples: Depending on how you look at it, failure is also a good experience.
Depending on how you look at it, this picture also looks like a human face.
Depending on how you use it, this tool can be very handy.

fields.meaning: Whether or not… (ようと～まいと)
fields.connection: V (V volitional form) + と + V + まいと が + V + まいが / How to use まい るV -> Vるまい / V ます まい うV -> Vるまい くる -> こまい / くるまい する -> しまい / すまい / するまい
examples: Whether it rains or not, we'll leave as planned.
Whether he comes or not, we'll start the meeting.
Whether people believe it or not, this is a fact.

fields.meaning: …, you know; …, OK (male speech sentence-final particle, emphasis: ぞ/ぜ)
examples: All right, let's go!
If you're late, I'm leaving without you.
This is an important match, you know.
